{{short description|Israeli-Swiss writer and mathematician}}
'''George Geza Szpiro''' ({{Langx|he|ג'ורג' גזה שפירא}}; born 18 February 1950 in [[Vienna]])<ref>''[[Marquis Who's Who|Who's Who in Finance and Industry]] 1998–1999'', p. 781</ref> is an Israeli–Swiss author, journalist, and mathematician. He has written articles and books on [[popular mathematics]] and related topics.

==Life and career==
Szpiro was born in Vienna in 1950, and moved to [[Zug]], Switzerland, in 1961.<ref name="NZZ" /> He obtained a [[master's degree]] in mathematics and physics from [[ETH Zurich]].  He also obtained an [[Master of Business Administration|MBA]] from [[Stanford University]], in 1975.<ref name="NZZ" /> Afterward, he worked as a [[management consultant]] at [[McKinsey & Company]].<ref name="TUB">"[http://presseservice.pressrelations.de/pressemitteilung/deutsche-mathematikervereinigung-verleiht-medienpreise-255198.html Deutsche Mathematiker-Vereinigung verleiht Medienpreise]", Press Release, [[Technische Universität Berlin]] (2006-11-06)</ref><ref name="DMV" /> In 1984, he obtained a Ph.D. in [[mathematical economics]] from [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem|Hebrew University]].<ref name="NZZ">{{citation |title=''George G. Szpiro - NZZ'' |url=http://www.nzz.ch/impressum/impressum_szpiro_george_g_1.194291 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150412092042/http://www.nzz.ch/impressum/impressum_szpiro_george_g_1.194291 |archive-date=2015-04-12}}</ref><ref name="DMV" />

Szpiro was an assistant professor at the [[Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania]], during 1984–1986. He was a lecturer in mathematical economics at Hebrew University, during 1986–1992. He also taught at the [[University of Zurich]].<ref name="TUB" /><ref name="DMV" /> He has published research papers related to mathematics, finance, and statistics.<ref name="RG">"[https://www.researchgate.net/profile/George_Szpiro/publications George G. Szpiro - Publications]"—list of Szpiro's publications at [[ResearchGate]]</ref>

Since 1986, Szpiro has worked as a journalist at ''[[Neue Zürcher Zeitung]]''.<ref name="NZZ" /> At ''NZZ'', he has been the Israel [[correspondent]] and mathematics [[columnist]].<ref name="NZZ" /><ref name="NAMS">{{citation |first=G. |last=Szpiro |title=Interview with Stephen Smale |journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] |date=2007 |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200708/tx070800995p.pdf |volume=54 |pages=995–997}}</ref> For his mathematics columns, Szpiro was awarded the Prix Média by the [[Swiss Academy of Natural Sciences]], in 2003.<ref>"[https://naturalsciences.ch/organisations/scnat/auszeichnungen/prix_media/laureates Preisträger Prix Média]", Swiss Academy of Natural Sciences</ref><ref>[http://ec.europa.eu/research/science-awards/pdf/descartes_comm_brochure05.pdf ''Descartes Communication Prize''], [[Directorate-General for Research and Innovation (European Commission)]] (2005)</ref> He was also awarded the Media Prize by the [[German Mathematical Society]], in 2006.<ref name="DMV">{{citation |title=''Medienpreise der DMV 2006'' |url=http://www.mathematik.de/ger/presse/dmvmedienpreis/dmvmedienpreise2006.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090123100309/http://www.mathematik.de/ger/presse/dmvmedienpreis/dmvmedienpreise2006.html |archive-date=2009-01-23}}</ref> Beside writing for ''NZZ'', he has also written non-research mathematics columns for journals such as ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' and ''[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]''.<ref name="RG" /><ref name="NAMS" />

==Books==
*  ''Kepler's Conjecture: How Some of the Greatest Minds in History Helped Solve One of the Oldest Math Problems in the World'' ([[John Wiley & Sons]], 2003)
* ''The Secret Life of Numbers: 50 Easy Pieces on How Mathematicians Work and Think'' ([[Joseph Henry Press]], 2006) 
* ''Poincaré's Prize: The Hundred-Year Quest to Solve One of Math's Greatest Puzzles'' ([[Dutton Penguin|Dutton]], 2007) 
* ''Numbers Rule: The Vexing Mathematics of Democracy, from Plato to the Present'' ([[Princeton University Press]], 2010) 
* ''A Mathematical Medley: Fifty Easy Pieces on Mathematics'' ([[American Mathematical Society]], 2010) 
* ''Pricing the Future: Finance, Physics, and the 300-year Journey to the Black-Scholes Equation'' ([[Basic Books]], 2011)
